title: Price’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage, with new thematic material rather than recognisable existing melodies.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.
notes: the pasted batch brief is summarised in brackets; the last sentence is verbatim

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Price’s Missing Symphony (work id price-symphony-1)

Florence Price wrote four symphonies (in E minor, G minor — now lost —, C minor and D minor). This is a new symphony in A flat major in her manner. It is not a reconstruction of the lost Second Symphony or of anything else of hers, and no theme is taken from her or from any spiritual.

Orchestra (13 staves, sounding pitch): pairs of flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons, four horns, two trumpets, three trombones and tuba (one staff), timpani in A flat and E flat, strings.

Her symphonies join the late-Romantic symphony she learned in Boston to the music she grew up with. The features taken up here: themes built on the five-note (pentatonic) scale, in the manner of spirituals but newly written; call and response between solo instruments; a slow movement that is a hymn for the brass choir answered by the woodwind; a “Juba” — the syncopated plantation dance she used in place of a scherzo — as third movement; and a fast, short finale in 6/8.

Movements
I. Andante – Allegro ma non troppo, A flat: a horn call; a broad pentatonic main theme; a second theme in C minor given as call and response between oboe and clarinet; in the reprise it returns in F minor.
II. Largo, D flat: a newly written hymn for trumpets, horns and trombones, with woodwind responses and a middle section for strings and clarinet in B flat minor.
III. Juba: Allegro, A flat, 2/4: a syncopated tune over a steady off-beat accompaniment, with a gentler trio in D flat.
IV. Finale: Presto, A flat, 6/8: a rondo in constant motion.

Target length about fourteen minutes. Compromise known from the start: every tune, the hymn and the chord of every bar are written by hand; a program scores quiet, woodwind and full-orchestra passages from the chord plan.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m1: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. First movement. The first build reported 68 half-step clashes, nearly all where a pentatonic melody note met the seventh of a chord in the accompaniment (the chords were simplified to triads there), and eight parallels with the bass, removed by changing inversions.

entries.text: Build m2, m3, m4: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. Movements II–IV. Fixes after the first build: in the hymn, a melody note a sixth above the bass was sounding against the chord's seventh (the seventh was removed); eight parallel octaves/fifths between first violins and bass; one bar of the Juba's trio rewritten; the timpani of the slow movement retuned to D flat and A flat.
